title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Abducting and Trafficking Women and Children

articles.content_en: Deceiving or luring infants or young children to separate them from their guardians or caretakers shall be deemed as "stealing infants or young children" as stipulated in Article 240, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Where a staff member of a medical institution, social welfare institution, or other unit, for the purpose of illegal profit, sells a child under their medical treatment, care, or custody to another person, they shall be convicted and punished for the crime of trafficking children.

Where a person, under the pretext of arranging a marriage, by means of illegally seizing identity documents, restricting personal freedom, or taking advantage of the woman's unfamiliarity with the local conditions, language barriers, isolation, or helplessness, against the woman's will, sells her to another person, criminal liability shall be investigated for the crime of trafficking women.
Where a person, under the pretext of arranging a marriage, colludes with the introduced woman to defraud another person of money or property, and the amount is relatively large, criminal liability shall be investigated for the crime of fraud.

Where, when state functionaries are screening children of unknown origin or conducting a rescue operation, a person hides, transfers, or engages in other acts that obstruct the rescue of a purchased child, and after persuasion and education still fails to cooperate, this shall constitute "hindering the rescue" as stipulated in Article 241, paragraph 6 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

Where a purchaser of an abducted woman has formed a stable marital and family relationship with her, and at the time of rescue the purchased woman voluntarily remains in the locality to live together, it may be deemed as "in accordance with the purchased woman's will, not hindering her return to her original place of residence".

Where a person who purchases an abducted woman or child subsequently organizes or forces prostitution, organizes begging, or engages in activities that violate public security administration, thereby constituting another crime, the punishment shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions on combined punishment for multiple crimes.

Where a person who purchases an abducted woman or child also uses violence or threats to obstruct state functionaries from rescuing the purchased woman or child, or gathers a crowd to obstruct state functionaries from rescuing the purchased woman or child, and constitutes the crime of obstructing public service or the crime of gathering a crowd to obstruct the rescue of purchased women or children, the punishment shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions on combined punishment for multiple crimes.

Where a person purchases an abducted woman for the purpose of marriage, or purchases an abducted child for the purpose of raising, and involves multiple family members or relatives and friends in the participation, the person who plays a primary role shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

The term "child" as used in Articles 240 and 241 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China means a person under the age of 14. Among them, a person under one year of age is an infant, and a person one year of age or older but under six years of age is a young child.
This Interpretation shall come into force as of January 1, 2017.
